title_override: Tungnath in May: 8–18°C, rhododendrons in bloom
meta_description_override: May is Tungnath's best month — 8–18°C, rhododendrons blazing along the trail and a clear Chandrashila summit. NakshIQ verdict: 5/5.

title_override: Nainital in May: 15–25°C, but peak crowds
meta_description_override: Weather's perfect at 15–25°C — the lake isn't. 60–90 min boat queues, tripled room rates, parking full by 9am. Mukteshwar stays calmer.

title_override: Kasauli in May: 18–30°C, pleasant midweek
meta_description_override: Warm 18–30°C and pleasant, but plains families pack Mall Road and Monkey Point on weekends. Come midweek and book ahead. Verdict: 4/5.

title_override: Kochi in May: 28–34°C, humid and squally
meta_description_override: 28–34°C, 85% humidity and pre-monsoon squalls — Kochi's heaviest stretch. Hotel rates bottom out mid-month if you go anyway. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Mahabaleshwar in June: monsoon shuts viewpoints
meta_description_override: Heavy monsoon sets in — viewpoints closed and landslide risk on the ghat roads. June starts the hill-station shutdown; plan for October instead.

title_override: Bhopal in June: pre-monsoon peak heat
meta_description_override: June is Bhopal's pre-monsoon peak — dry, punishing heat before the rains. The lakes, Bhojpur shivling and Bhimbetka reward an Oct–March visit.

title_override: Dhanaulti in May: 14–25°C, camps running
meta_description_override: Warm 14–25°C with every campsite open — and a weekend rush from Delhi. Come midweek and book ahead. NakshIQ verdict: 4/5.

title_override: Valparai in May: 19–30°C, clear till mid-month
meta_description_override: The first fortnight is workable at 19–30°C; the last 10 days bring the SW monsoon and landslide-watch on the 40-hairpin road. Verdict: 3/5.

title_override: Kalpa in June: 14–25°C, clear before the 20th
meta_description_override: June opens pleasant at 14–25°C with clear Kinner Kailash views — until the monsoon's leading edge arrives around the 20th. Verdict: 5/5.

title_override: Jaipur in July: monsoon arrives, forts slippery
meta_description_override: The monsoon reaches Jaipur — cooler than peak summer but humid, and the forts turn slippery underfoot. Pleasant light, awkward sightseeing. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Chakrata in May: 14–26°C, all trails open
meta_description_override: Clear skies at 14–26°C with every trail open — Tiger Falls, the Budher caves and Deoban forest all in reach. Book ahead. Verdict: 4/5.

title_override: Somnath in June: humid, squally pre-monsoon
meta_description_override: Pre-monsoon humidity and incoming squalls on the Arabian Sea coast — Jyotirlinga darshan still works, the open Triveni ghat doesn't. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Yercaud in June: 16–25°C, monsoon onset
meta_description_override: The SW monsoon arrives — 16–25°C and 100–200mm rain, lighter than the Western Ghats but enough to fog Lady's Seat by afternoon. Verdict: 3/5.

title_override: Pachmarhi in May: 35–42°C, waterfalls dry
meta_description_override: At 35–42°C the forest hikes are brutal by 10am and every waterfall is bone-dry. Pachmarhi's shade and water are gone — wait for July. Verdict: 1/5.

title_override: Udupi in May: 28–34°C, Malpe ferry closes
meta_description_override: Peak pre-monsoon — 28–34°C, 82% humidity, a building sea swell and thunderstorms, with the Malpe ferry closing mid-month. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Lambasingi in May: 15–27°C, thundershowers
meta_description_override: Cool for the South at 15–27°C, but pre-monsoon thundershowers, 60–100mm of rain and marginal roads. Upside: room rates at a year-low.

title_override: Gokarna in May: 28–34°C, cliff beaches close
meta_description_override: Peak pre-monsoon at 28–34°C and 82% humidity — the cliff beaches close as the sea swell builds and thunderstorms roll in. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Dharamshala in June: 18–30°C, hazy peaks
meta_description_override: Pre-monsoon haze at 18–30°C leaves Dhauladhar views unreliable, with daily thunderstorms. Triund still works with rain gear. Verdict: 3/5.

title_override: Chakrata in June: 16–28°C, Tiger Falls roaring
meta_description_override: Pre-monsoon 16–28°C, Tiger Falls roaring on snowmelt and forest trails still good early-month — but hazier views and passing storms. Verdict: 3/5.

title_override: Kukke Subramanya in May: trek closes mid-month
meta_description_override: Peak pre-monsoon — 25–33°C, 82% humidity and thunderstorms, with the Kumara Parvatha trek closing mid-month. The temple stays open.

title_override: Kabini in May: 20–35°C, elephant super-herds
meta_description_override: May is Kabini's wildlife peak — 200–500+ elephants gather along the receding backwaters as the heat concentrates them at water. Verdict: 5/5.

title_override: Gurez Valley in June: 10–25°C, road just open
meta_description_override: The valley opens for the season — 10–25°C, wildflower meadows and the turquoise Kishanganga. ILP required, basic homestays only. Verdict: 5/5.

title_override: Dharmasthala in May: 25–34°C, midday queues
meta_description_override: Peak pre-monsoon at 25–34°C and 82% humidity, with thunderstorms and brutal midday darshan queues. Arrive early. NakshIQ verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Mangalore in May: 28–35°C, rough seas
meta_description_override: Peak pre-monsoon — 28–35°C, 82% humidity and a rough sea, with thunderstorms through the last 10 days of the month. Verdict: 2/5.

title_override: Barot Valley in June: 15–27°C, last clear window
meta_description_override: The first half is the last clear window before the rains — 15–27°C, the Uhl River rising and light showers from late June. Verdict: 4/5.

title_override: Tirthan Valley in June: 18–28°C, last trek window
meta_description_override: Pre-monsoon 18–28°C — the last window for Great Himalayan NP treks before the rains, though afternoons run hot and the river swells. Verdict: 4/5.

title_override: जून में तुंगनाथ: 10–20°C, हरे-भरे बुग्याल
meta_description_override: ट्रेकिंग के लिए बढ़िया — 10–20°C, बुग्याल हरियाली से ढके और चंद्रशिला शिखर के साफ़ दृश्य। दोपहर बाद मानसून-पूर्व बादल घिरते हैं। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 4/5।

title_override: जून में जबलपुर: 28–42°C, गर्मी और उमस
meta_description_override: मानसून-पूर्व का कठिन दौर — 28–42°C, भीषण गर्मी के साथ तेज़ उमस। भेड़ाघाट की संगमरमर चट्टानें अक्टूबर–मार्च में बेहतर। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 2/5।

title_override: जून में रामेश्वरम्: 27–34°C, समुद्री हवा लौटी
meta_description_override: दक्षिण-पश्चिम मानसून की फुहारें गर्मी कुछ कम करती हैं — 27–34°C, समुद्री हवा लौटती है और मंदिर पूरे अनुष्ठान-क्रम में रहता है। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 3/5।

title_override: मई में ग्वालियर: 41–46°C, खुला किला तपता
meta_description_override: 41–46°C — ग्वालियर का सबसे तपता महीना। रॉक-कट ग्वालियर किला, सास-बहू मंदिर और तेली का मंदिर — कहीं छाँव नहीं। अक्टूबर–मार्च बेहतर। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 1/5।

title_override: मई में यमुनोत्री: 8–20°C, चारधाम सीज़न चरम
meta_description_override: मंदिर खुला, सबसे अच्छा मौसम 8–20°C — चारधाम सीज़न का चरम। जानकी चट्टी से 6 किमी की चढ़ाई आरामदेह, मंदिर पर गर्म जलकुंड। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 5/5।

title_override: जून में लोनावला: मानसून और झरने शुरू
meta_description_override: मानसून आते ही लोनावला बदल जाता है — झरने फूटने लगते हैं, घाटी हरी हो जाती है। पहला हफ़्ता हल्का, मध्य जून से असली जादू। NakshIQ रेटिंग: 4/5।
